headline: Iran war caused Republican midterm losses, Trump acknowledges but defends decision
summary: President Donald Trump stated that the Iran war, which led to a spike in gasoline prices, was a significant factor in the Republican party's losses in the US midterm elections. Despite this, he maintained the war was necessary to prevent Iran from acquiring nu
details: President Donald Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the Iran war played a role in his Republican party losing control of Congress in the US midterm elections. He stated, however, that the conflict was a necessary undertaking.

Trump attributed the Republican losses primarily to the Iran war's impact on gasoline prices, which significantly influenced voters. This surge in prices was seen as a strong factor behind the Democrats' substantial gains.
He defended the war, asserting that it was essential to prevent Tehran from developing a nuclear weapon. Trump emphasized that he would not have acted differently regarding the conflict.

The former president also expressed agreement with Vice President JD Vance's social media post, which cited the war as the reason for deep electoral losses. Trump maintained his stance despite the electoral consequences.

Furthermore, Trump reiterated his belief that if he had been on the ballot, the Republicans would have won. He suggested that the 'love' observed at his rallies could not be successfully transferred to other candidates.
caption:
Former President Trump admitted the Iran war contributed to Republican losses in the US midterm elections, yet he defended the decision.

President Donald Trump acknowledged on Wednesday that the Iran war played a role in his Republican party losing control of Congress in the US midterm elections. He stated, however, that the conflict was a necessary undertaking.

Trump attributed the Republican losses primarily to the Iran war's impact on gasoline prices, which significantly influenced voters. This surge in prices was seen as a strong factor behind the Democrats' substantial gains.

He defended the war, asserting that it was essential to prevent Tehran from developing a nuclear weapon. Trump emphasized that he would not have acted differently regarding the conflict.

The former president also expressed agreement with Vice President JD Vance's social media post, which cited the war as the reason for deep electoral losses. Trump maintained his stance despite the electoral consequences.

Furthermore, Trump reiterated his belief that if he had been on the ballot, the Republicans would have won. He suggested that the 'love' observed at his rallies could not be successfully transferred to other candidates.

headline_marked: [[Pitch uncertainty looms]] for Bangladesh ahead of second Test against West Indies in Sylhet
headline: Pitch uncertainty looms for Bangladesh ahead of second Test against West Indies in Sylhet
summary: Despite team management's request for a spin-friendly track, weather conditions in Sylhet suggest a more sporting surface, potentially leading to a three-pronged pace attack for Bangladesh.
details: Bangladesh Cricket Board's head of turf management, Tony Hemming, closely inspected the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium pitch yesterday afternoon, with the second Test against West Indies beginning today.

The host team's expectation of another spin-friendly surface may be challenged by the reality of the conditions. Sources indicate the team requested a turning track, but hot and overcast weather has prevented the sun from baking the surface.

Even within the Bangladesh camp, there is skepticism about relying heavily on spin, especially after their struggles in Mirpur. Head coach Phil Simmons hinted at a 'good cricket wicket' similar to a Pakistan wicket seen earlier.

A three-pronged pace attack is now a possibility, though team management sources remain cautious. Simmons also raised concerns about left-arm spinner Taijul Islam's form, who has taken only five wickets in his last four Tests.
Bangladesh's greater worry remains their batting. Simmons suggested a top-order reshuffle following Mominul Haque's absence, with Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto expected to move to number three.
Mushfiqur Rahim and Tawhid Hridoy could occupy the next two positions. Litton Das has struggled with a tennis elbow injury during training but is expected to retain his place if fit.

West Indies head coach Darren Sammy stated his team prepared for a pace-friendly surface, noting Bangladesh's fast bowlers impressed in Australia. He mentioned having Kemar Roach ready if the wicket favors seam.
Simmons remained tight-lipped about Bangladesh's final combination. Regardless of the pitch, the Tigers must bat better to achieve a positive outcome in the Sylhet Test.
